title.narrative: Sustainable Rural Infrastructure Development Project in Northern Mountain Provinces

description.narrative: The project will rehabilitate and upgrade deteriorated but critical rural infrastructure in 15 mountainous provinces of northern Viet Nam. These provinces have a combined population of 12.2 million people and are among the poorest in the country. Overall poverty rates average about 27%, but are considerably higher in more isolated areas, where poverty levels may be 50%-60%. One of the main reasons for these high levels of poverty is limited access to productive assets and infrastructure (such as irrigation water systems), and physical isolation. The project will focus on improving small- to medium-scale irrigation and/or drainage systems, rural roads, and district and commune markets. The project will include 40-45 subprojects. Rehabilitation and upgrading of rural infrastructure is expected to have a positive impact on the lives and livelihoods of the population in the project area, providing easier access to inputs (including irrigation water), markets, health services, higher levels of education, and employment opportunities, while reducing production and marketing costs.

11,849 ha of irrigated land either receiving water in a timely manner and in the quantities required or being drained of surplus flood water in a timely manner. Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Actual value:

Output: 1. Priority rural infrastructure rehabilitated or upgraded Indicator: 1.2. 460 km of rural road grades type A, IV, V, and VI rehabilitated by 2016 Progress/Status: 466 km of rural road grades Type A, IV, V, and VI were rehabilitated. Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Actual value:

Output: 1. Priority rural infrastructure rehabilitated or upgraded Indicator: 1.3. 15,000 households provided with clean water by 2016. Progress/Status: 16,097 households have been provided with clean water.
Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Actual value:

Output: 1. Priority rural infrastructure rehabilitated or upgraded Indicator: 1.4. 2 rural commune markets upgraded or established by commissioning but not later than 2016. Progress/Status: 5 rural commune markets were upgraded or established. Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Actual value:

Output: 1. Priority rural infrastructure rehabilitated or upgraded Indicator: 1.6. The works generate a minimum of $10 million worth of employment, of which 25% is for women by 2015. Progress/Status: The works generate $20.78 million equivalent worth of employment, of which 25% is for women. Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Actual value:

Output: 2. Improved capacities for project management and for rural infrastructure use and sustainability Indicator: 2.1. 12 Operation and maintenance asset management plans (for irrigation subprojects) prepared and adopted; plans to include strategies for using local labor-based methods, with 25% participation by women by 2015 Progress/Status: 12 operation and maintenance asset management plans (for 10 irrigation and 2 embankment subprojects) have been adopted; the plans include strategies for using local labor-based methods, with 25% participation by women. Data Source: Project implementation monitoring Actual value:

Output: 2. Improved capacities for project management and for rural infrastructure use and sustainability Indicator: 2.4. 115 civil works packages undertaken in a timely manner in accordance with agreed schedules and by 2015 Progress/Status: All 110 civil works contracts (81 of Loan 2682 and 29 of Loan 2683) were completed but many were delayed in comparison with the agreed schedules and by June 2017. Data Source: Project implementation monitoring Actual value:

Output: 1. Priority rural infrastructure rehabilitated or upgraded Indicator: 1.5. All market improvements include facilities for women by 2015. Progress/Status: All markets have included facilities for women. Data Source: Project-funded baseline surveys Project implementation monitoring and PBME studies Provincial statistics Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved capacities for project management and for rural infrastructure use and sustainability Indicator: 2.2. Road safety campaign carried out with counterpart financing under parallel national program. Progress/Status: Road safety campaign carried out in most project areas with counterpart financing under parallel national program. Data Source: Project implementation monitoring Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved capacities for project management and for rural infrastructure use and sustainability Indicator: 2.3. All CPMU and PPMU staff trained in ADB procedures. Progress/Status: All 169 staff (including 18 women staff) of CPMU and 15 PPMUs were trained in ADB procedures and operation of infrastructure. Data Source: Project implementation monitoring Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2013 Target value: Y
The intended outcome is to increase access to, and use of priority rural infrastructure by the poor and ethnic minorities in the project area.

1.2. Cropping intensity in irrigation command areas increased by 30% after commissioning and no later than 2017 Progress/Status: In 2015, average cropping intensity in irrigation areas was estimated at 1.94, an increase of 78% over 2011. Data Source: Department of Agricultural and Rural Development statistics Base year: 2011 Baseline value: N

2. Roads and markets
2.1. Producer surplus increased by 20% by 2017 - induced by increased farm-gate market prices for agricultural produce and greater access to production inputs Progress/Status: In 2015, producer surplus (for rice production) in project area averages D2.22 million per ton, a 38% increase over 2011. Data Source: Department of Agricultural and Rural Development statistics Base year: 2011 Baseline value: N

2.2 Travel indicators: VOC reduced by 60%; travel time reduced by 50%; traffic volume increased by 200% by 2017 Progress/Status: Data for all three indicators were not available in the statistics of provincial Departments of Transport (DOTs) as assumed at appraisal because DOTs have not collected these data for project roads. The supplementary data was not collected by the BME consultants because they mobilized in May 2013, while data required were for 2011. Data Source: Provincial Department of Transport statistics Base year: 2011 Baseline value: N

2.3. Within one year of subproject completion: Average increase in annual traffic 8% in tons and 7% in ton-km, of which 60% will be agricultural surpluses Progress/Status: During 2011 to 2015 volume of freight estimated to have increased 18% per year in tons and 6% per year in ton-km. There is no data available for agricultural surpluses. Data Source: Provincial Department of Transport statistics Base year: 2011 Baseline value: N

2.4. Within one year of subproject completion: Average increase in passenger volumes: 12% in passengers and 10% in passenger-km Progress/Status: 2011-2015 passenger volume estimated to have increased 28% per year in passengers and 45% per year in passenger-km. Data Source: Provincial Department of Transport statistics Base year: 2011 Baseline value: N
